analysis.investment_thesis: At a P/E of 109 and P/B of 4.66, Aegis Vopak trades at roughly 6x my Graham Number (~₹33 vs market ₹201) with no multi-year earnings history — the 2022 revenue was zero and net profit only turned meaningful in FY24. This is a recently-listed, capex-heavy terminalling venture priced as a growth story; there is no margin of safety whatsoever.
key_strengths: Tangible infrastructure asset base (terminals, storage) backing equity of ₹4,742 Cr
Operating cash flow turned meaningfully positive (₹478 Cr in FY25) and FCF positive first time
Debt/Equity dropped to 0.42 post-IPO equity infusion — balance sheet de-risked
key_risks: P/E 109, P/B 4.66, EV/EBITDA 55.8 — speculative premium with zero margin of safety
Only 2 years of real profits (FY24 ₹87 Cr, FY25 ₹127 Cr); fails my 5-year earnings test
Finance cost ₹193 Cr vs operating income ₹458 Cr — interest coverage only ~2.4x, below my 3.5x floor
red_flags: Fresh IPO with sellers (promoter Aegis/Vopak JV) setting price — inherent information asymmetry
ROCE of 7.01% is below cost of debt — capital is not yet earning its keep
Negative cumulative FCF over 2022-2024; profitability is unproven through a cycle
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a strict Graham lens, this security fails nearly every quantitative filter I apply. The Graham Number using FY25 EPS ~₹1.15 and BVPS ~₹42.9 computes to approximately ₹33; the market asks ₹201 — a sixfold premium over defensive value. P/E of 109 and P/S of 31 imply the market has already capitalised a decade of flawless execution. The earnings record is too short (meaningful profit only since FY24) to establish "proven earning power," and interest coverage of ~2.4x (EBIT 458 / Finance cost 193) sits below my 3.5x threshold, leaving little cushion if throughput or tariffs soften.

The business itself — regulated LPG/chemical terminalling with a strong promoter (86.94%) and Royal Vopak parentage — is not without merit; tangible assets and 48% operating margins are real. But Mr. Market is pricing it as a utility-plus-growth hybrid while the financials still resemble a start-up: ₹7,072 Cr of assets generating just ₹127 Cr of profit (1.8% ROA), with ROCE of 7% below even Indian sovereign yields. I would require the price to fall below book value (~₹43) and at least three more years of clean earnings before considering this. Until then: avoid.
